claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has coercivity below 20 Oe.
Suppression of the orbital moment causes the initial alloy's low coercivity and soft-magnetic behavior.
The baseline single-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has a Curie temperature above 400 K.
Aging at 600-800 °C for 10-100 hours will induce nanoscale Ti-rich Ti2Ni or TiFe precipitates in the fcc matrix.
Adding excess Ti at 10-20 at.% will promote in-situ precipitation during solidification.
The desired microstructure contains 5-15 vol% Ti-rich intermetallic precipitates within an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The Ti-rich precipitates will be 5-50 nm in size.
Ti-rich precipitates act as strong magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Strain fields around the precipitates enhance spin-orbit coupling and restore an orbital-moment contribution to magnetic anisotropy.
Chemical-potential gradients and localized strain fields generated by the precipitates pin domain walls and thereby increase coercivity.
Interfaces between the fcc matrix and the intermetallic phase modify electronic structure and enhance the orbital magnetic moment.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have coercivity exceeding 100 Oe.
The precipitate-containing alloy will maintain saturation magnetization above 60 emu/g.
The alloy will retain a Curie temperature above 500 K because the dominant fcc matrix has strong ferromagnetic exchange interactions.
The processed alloy will retain an fcc matrix while developing a secondary Ti-rich intermetallic phase.
The design is applicable for Ti concentrations of 5-20 at.% and aging temperatures of 600-800 °C.
Ti concentrations above 25 at.% may generate excessive brittle phases or destroy fcc-matrix continuity, reducing magnetic performance.
A dual-phase sample with coercivity below 50 Oe would falsify the proposed coercivity enhancement.
Failure to observe orbital-moment enhancement by XMCD in the dual-phase sample would invalidate the proposed orbital-restoration mechanism.

contradictions.description: An equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni-Ti starting alloy implies approximately 25 at.% Ti, whereas the intervention calls 10-20 at.% Ti 'excess Ti' and the stated applicability range is only 5-20 at.%. These composition descriptions cannot all characterize the same nominal starting/design range.
